body:
_Migrated from issue #1375, filed 2026-08-04._

Observed while investigating #1372. Filing with the evidence I actually have — I have **not** reproduced this deliberately, so treat the mechanism as unconfirmed.

## What I saw

On a running `cwn-local` (container up ~4h, `metadata-change-detector` up and healthy), the change-log folder held a file that was **2 hours old**:

```
/app/calibre-web-automated/metadata_change_logs/
-rw-r--r-- 1 abc dialout  286 Aug  4 08:20 20260804082046-221.json
```

Contents were a real tags edit on book 221. The container had started at roughly 06:20, so this log was written at 08:20 **while the watcher was already running** — it is not a leftover from before boot.

It stayed there untouched until 10:21, when I made an unrelated metadata edit on a different book. At that point the detector processed *both*:

```
[metadata-change-detector] New file detected: 20260804082046-221.json
[metadata-change-detector] New file detected: 20260804102056-176.json
```

So book 221's edit was applied to its files roughly two hours late, and only because someone happened to edit a different book.

## Why it matters

The user-visible symptom is identical to #1372 — you edit metadata, the library updates, the file does not — except it resolves on its own later, which makes it harder to recognise. If nobody edits another book, the change never lands.

## What I have not established

Whether this is a dropped watcher event (inotify or the polling fallback missing a `close_write`), something in the debounce/cooldown in `scripts/metadata_change_dispatch.py` (`CWA_DETECTOR_DEBOUNCE=1.0`, `CWA_DETECTOR_COOLDOWN=15.0`), or an environment quirk of this host. Note this instance takes the **polling** fallback, because the run script prefers polling under Docker Desktop.

The shape resembles the ingest bug fixed in #1362 — a pending item waiting on an unrelated later event rather than being swept — but on a different service, so that is a hint, not a diagnosis.

## Suggested first step

Reproduce by writing a change log directly into the folder while the detector runs, on both the inotify and polling paths, and see whether it is picked up on its own. If not, a periodic sweep of the folder would bound the delay the same way #1362's startup sweep did for ingest.
title: [bug] A metadata change log can sit unprocessed until an unrelated edit arrives
